ARMED FORCES ACT 1972

ARMED FORCES

(TERMS OF SERVICE OF REGULAR FORCES) REGULATIONS 2013

IN exercise of the powers conferred by sections 15 and 36 of the Armed Forces Act 1972

[Act 77], the Armed Forces Council, with the approval of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong,

makes the following regulations:

PART I

GENERAL

Citation

1. These regulations may be cited as the Armed Forces (Terms of Service of

Regular Forces) Regulations 2013.

Application

2. These Regulations shall apply to all officers and servicemen of the regular forces.

Interpretation

3. In these Regulations, unless the context otherwise requires—

"Act" means the Armed Forces Act 1972 [Act 77];

"child" means a child of a member—

(a) who is below the age of twenty-one years and includes—

(i) a posthumous child, a dependant step-child or an

illegitimate child conceived before the death of the

member; and

(ii) a child adopted before the death of the member, under any

written law, custom or usage; or

(b) of any age, who is mentally retarded or physically and

permanently incapacitated and incapable of supporting himself;

"member" means an officer or a serviceman of the regular forces;

"submarine crew" means a member who has passed the submarine qualifying

course and has not been suspended or removed from his qualification, serves in a

submarine or performs duties in relation to the duties of the submarine;

"aircrew" includes a pilot, navigator, flight engineer, weapon sensor operator, air

tactical coordinator, air quartermaster, air steward and air stewardess who performs

aviation duties in a unit of the Armed Forces of Malaysia;

"seaman branch" means a branch in the Royal Malaysian Navy;

"medical leave" means—

(a) a period of leave not exceeding fourteen days granted to a member

upon the recommendation of a medical officer; or

(b) a period of leave exceeding fourteen days granted to a member

upon the recommendation of a Medical Board;

"hospital" means any Government hospital, Armed Forces Hospital and includes

any university hospital, Government clinic and any Government medical institution;

"family" means the husband or wife and children of a member;

"Selection Board" means a board established by the Armed Forces Council which

is responsible for the selection of members of the regular forces for any specific purpose

in accordance with Perintah Majlis Angkatan Tentera;

"Medical Board" means a board consisting of not less than two medical officers in

the related field established by the competent authority;

"enter into service", in relation to—

(a) an officer, means a person who is qualified to be commissioned

under section 6 of the Act; and

(b) a serviceman, means a person who is qualified to be enlisted under

section 18 of the Act;

"substantive rank" means a rank granted to an officer or a serviceman other than

acting rank or local rank;

"local rank" means a rank granted to an officer or a serviceman for the purpose

of discharging duties in an appointment which requires a rank higher than his

substantive rank;

"medical officer" means a registered medical practitioner or a dental

practitioner in the civil service or in the Armed Forces of Malaysia service;

"General Duty List Officer" means any officer other than a Professional Duty List

Officer or a Special Duty List Officer;

"Professional Duty List Officer" means an officer holding a professional

qualification and commissioned into the Professional Duty List;

"Special Duty List Officer" means a serviceman in a particular field of skill who

has been commissioned into the Special Duty List;

"seaman" means a person who is registered in the seaman branch;

"guardian", in relation to a child, means any person or association or persons,

other than his natural parents, who has legal custody of the child according to the law;

"recruit" means a person enlisted in accordance with the provisions of these

Regulations who has not completed his basic training for a period of six months or any

other period as determined by the competent authority;

"organisation" includes a body or a corporation and any subsidiary of such body

or corporation.

Equivalent rank

4. Any reference made to a rank in the Malaysian Army shall be construed as a

reference to the equivalent rank in the Royal Malaysian Navy and the Royal Malaysian

Air Force, as the case may be, as specified in the First Schedule.

PART II

OFFICERS AND SERVICEMEN

Qualification to enter into service

5. (1) Any person who is a citizen of Malaysia may enter into the service of the

regular forces:

 Provided that only persons being Malays shall be allowed to enter the Royal

Malay Regiment.

(2) No person who has been discharged with disgrace, discharged or

terminated on the ground of discipline shall be commissioned, appointed, enlisted or reenlisted.

Miscellaneous qualifications for entry into service

6. (1) The miscellaneous qualifications for entry into the service of the regular

forces shall be in accordance with Perintah Majlis Angkatan Tentera.

(2) Notwithstanding anything contained in subregulation (1), the competent

authority may waive any or all of the miscellaneous qualifications for entry into service

if a state of war exists between the Yang di-Pertuan Agong and any foreign power or

while a Proclamation of Emergency issued by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong under Article

150 of the Federal Constitution is in force.

Entry selection test

7. (1) Every person who wishes to enter into the service of the regular forces

shall be required to undergo an entry selection test as determined by the competent

authority.

(2) No person shall enter into the service of the regular forces unless that

person has passed the entry selection test as specified under subregulation (1).

(3) This regulation shall not apply to a person or a class of persons exempted

by the competent authority.

Minimum medical standards for entry

8. The minimum medical standards required for entry into the service of the

regular forces shall be in accordance with Perintah Majlis Angkatan Tentera.

Medical examination

9. (1) Every person who wishes to enter into the service of the regular forces

shall undergo a medical examination by a medical officer to determine whether or not

his physical fitness and state of health meets the minimum medical standards as

specified in regulation 8.

(2) No person shall enter into the service of the regular forces unless he has

complied with the minimum medical standards as specified under regulation 8.

(3) Notwithstanding anything contained in subregulation (2), the Service

Chief may waive any or all of the minimum medical standards if a state of war exists

between the Yang di-Pertuan Agong and any foreign power or while a Proclamation of

Emergency issued by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong under Article 150 of the Federal

Constitution is in force.

Additional medical requirements for aircrew, submarine crew and seamen

10. (1) No person shall be an aircrew, submarine crew or a seaman unless he has

complied with the additional medical requirements which shall be in accordance with

Perintah Majlis Angkatan Tentera.

(2) Failure to comply with subregulation (1) shall not automatically bar such

person from rendering his service in other duties other than as an aircrew, submarine

crew or a seaman.

Medical standards while in service

11. (1) Every serving member shall comply with the medical standards which

shall be in accordance with Perintah Majlis Angkatan Tentera unless exempted

specifically by the Service Chief.

(2) A Medical Board shall be established for the purpose of determining the

state of health, degree of illness, fitness and capability of a member to perform his

official duties if the member does not comply with the medical standards specified in

subregulation (1).

(3) The Medical Board shall, if necessary, submit a recommendation to the

Service Chief, in the case of—

(a) an officer, for his retirement or termination of his service; or

(b) a serviceman, for his discharge from the service of the regular

forces,

pursuant to regulations 42, 43 and 61 respectively.

Security vetting

12. Every member shall, upon entering the service, undergo a security vetting, and if

found unfit, in the case of—

(a) an officer, be retired or terminated; or

(b) a serviceman, be discharged from the service of the regular forces,

as the case may be, with immediate effect.

Entry into service

13. (1) The entry of a member into the service of the regular forces shall

commence in the case of—

(a) an officer, on the date he is commissioned as an officer or

appointed as an officer cadet; and

(b) a serviceman, on the date he is enlisted.

(2) A member upon entering the service–

(a) of the Malaysian Army, in the case of—

(i) an officer, shall be commissioned; or

(ii) a serviceman, shall be enlisted to a corps or regiment of the

Malaysian Army; or

(b) of the Royal Malaysian Navy or of the Royal Malaysian Air Force,

 in the case of—

(i) an officer, shall be commissioned; or

(ii) a serviceman, shall be enlisted to a branch of the Royal

Malaysian Navy or the Royal Malaysian Air Force, as the

case may be.

(3) A person shall enter into the service of the regular forces as a member

through enlistment and attestation in accordance with section 18 of the Act, as specified

in the Second Schedule.

Rank, seniority and order of precedence

14. (1) The ranks to be conferred upon an officer or a serviceman in the regular

forces shall be as specified in the First Schedule.

(2) The seniority of an officer or a serviceman in the same rank shall be

reckoned from the date of his appointment to the substantive rank, or if he has been

granted an earlier date of seniority, his seniority shall be reckoned from the earlier date.

(3) An officer or a serviceman shall take precedence in accordance with his

substantive rank and his seniority in that rank.

Grant of local rank by Service Chief

15. (1) Notwithstanding any provisions in these Regulations, the Service Chief

may confer a local rank on any officer or serviceman—

(a) for a specific period; or

(b) to meet the needs that arise—

(i) when a conferment of a higher rank is necessary for the

purpose of status or seniority; or

(ii) to enable the discharge of duties in an appointment which

requires a rank higher than his substantive rank,

and at the end of such period of duty, such officer or serviceman shall be reverted to the

substantive rank held by him previously before the conferment of that local rank.

(2) The conferment of the local rank in subregulation (1) on any officer or

serviceman shall not affect the seniority of that officer or serviceman, and shall not be

deemed to be a promotion.

Transfer of a member

16. A member may be transferred from one Service to another Service or within the

same Service in accordance with sections 13 and 22 of the Act.

Postings

17. The postings of each member throughout his period of service shall be

determined in the case of—

(a) an officer, by a competent authority; and

(b) a serviceman, by the Service Chief.

Pay, allowance, pension and other benefits, etc.

18. (1) The pay, allowance and any other emoluments as determined from time

to time by the competent authority may be paid to a member in accordance with the

regulations made under section 157 of the Act.

(2) The pension, gratuity and other benefits as determined by the competent

authority may be paid to the members in accordance with the regulations made under

section 187 of the Act.

Leave

19. Every member is entitled for leave in accordance with Perintah Majlis Angkatan

Tentera.

Attachment or secondment of a member

20. (1) The competent authority may attach temporarily any member who is

posted in a corps or regiment or branch or in a particular Service, to a corps or regiment

or branch or another Service, or to another unit within the same Service.

(2) The Armed Forces Council may second any member in accordance with

Perintah Majlis Angkatan Tentera.

Period of service of a member on attachment or secondment outside service

21. (1) Any period of service of a member who is serving on attachment or

secondment outside the Service whether in or outside Malaysia pursuant to sections 5A,

5B and 5C of the Act shall be deemed to be a reckonable period of service in Malaysia for

the purpose of promotion and the seniority of such member.

(2) A member who is serving on attachment or secondment outside the

Service as specified in subregulation (1) shall be eligible for pay, allowance or any other

emoluments as determined from time to time by the competent authority in accordance

with the regulations made under section 157 of the Act.

(3) Any period of service of a member who is serving on attachment or

secondment outside the Service shall be recognized as a reckonable service.

Uniform

22. (1) Every member shall wear uniforms in accordance with Perintah Majlis

Angkatan Tentera.

(2) A member may wear on his uniform any badge conferred upon him in

accordance with Perintah Majlis Angkatan Tentera.

Badge

23. (1) The competent authority may, if it thinks reasonable, confer any badge to

any member who is eligible.

(2) The Armed Forces Council may determine the type, criteria and

qualification for wearing of badges and any other matters relating to it in Perintah

Majlis Angkatan Tentera.

Member may be required to undergo courses

24. (1) A member shall, when required by the competent authority, undergo

courses whether in or outside Malaysia.

(2) The competent authority may impose conditions on a member who has

been required to undergo any course under subregulation (1) to sign an agreement in

the form prescribed in Perintah Majlis Angkatan Tentera before the commencement of

such course for the purpose of determining the contractual period required to be

fulfilled by him upon the completion of such course, and such contractual period shall

include his actual period of full-time service.

(3) Notwithstanding any provisions in these Regulations, no member, other

than a short service commissioned officer, may undergo any course subject to the

condition imposed under subregulation (2) unless he has a sufficient period of service

in force to enable him to fulfill the obligations arising out of the agreement referred to in

subregulation (2).

Family may accompany member on long courses outside Malaysia

25. A member who is required to undergo a long course outside Malaysia may be

accompanied by his family throughout his period of study, and the member shall be

eligible to make any claim arising out of any expenditure incurred by him as approved

by the competent authority, in accordance with the regulations made under section 157

of the Act and Perintah Majlis Angkatan Tentera.

Transfer to the reserve

26. A member who has retired or completed his period of service in the regular

forces shall be transferred to the Regular Forces Reserve established under section 189

of the Act.

Reckoning of period of service

27. The rules for reckoning of service for the purpose of—

(a) discharge or re-engagement or transfer to the reserve shall be in

accordance with section 34 of the Act; and

(b) retirement benefits and other benefits shall be in accordance with the

regulations made under section 187 of the Act.

Retirement, discharge or retention in service beyond the date of retirement or

discharge due to medical grounds

28. (1) Subject to regulation 35, a member who is found below the prescribed

medical standards to perform his duties shall not be retained in the service after the

expiry date of his period of service but shall be retired or discharged from the service of

the regular forces.

(2) A member shall be retired or discharged if, within five months prior to the

discharge, such member becomes ill or sustains injury which causes him to be absent

from duties until the day before he is due for leave prior to the retirement or discharge.

(3) A member shall be discharged if he still has a remaining period of service

and is declared by a Medical Board to be unfit for further service due to disability.

Resettlement course

29. Subject to the approval of the Armed Forces Council, a member shall, at the end

of his period of service, undergo a resettlement course in accordance with Perintah

Majlis Angkatan Tentera.

Legal aid

30. A member who has been initiated with legal proceeding, during the exercise, or

arising from the performance, of his official duties, may be granted a legal aid by the

competent authority in accordance with Perintah Majlis Angkatan Tentera.

Promotion and seniority of a member who is missing while on duty, etc.

31. If a member is found missing while on duty, during a war, operation or training,

or has been detained as a prisoner of war, and his disappearance or detention was not

due to his non-compliance, insubordination or negligence—

(a) his seniority shall remain unaffected throughout his period of

disappearance or his detention;

(b) the member shall be eligible to be promoted, in the case of—

(i) an officer, by the Armed Forces Council with the consent of the

Yang di-Pertuan Agong; and

(ii) a serviceman, by the Service Chief,

if such promotion is beneficial to the armed forces.

Member who is absent from duties due to illness

32. (1) A member who is absent from duties because of illness shall upon the

certification of a medical officer, be eligible for full pay, allowance and any other

emoluments as determined by the competent authority.

(2) A member who is granted medical leave for a period exceeding eighteen

months upon the certification of a Medical Board shall not be eligible to receive any pay,

allowance or other emoluments, unless the Medical Board certifies that such member

has a chance to recover and is able to report for duty upon the expiry of such medical

leave.

Member who is on medical leave and has no chance to recover

33. (1) Subject to regulation 34, if a member who becomes ill, sustains injury or

suffers from disease is granted medical leave for a period exceeding eighteen months,

and a Medical Board certifies that the member has no chance to recover and is incapable

of reporting for duty upon the expiry of such medical leave, his Service Chief shall take

immediate action, in the case of—

(a) an officer, to retire or terminate his service; or

(b) a serviceman, to discharge him from the service of the regular

forces,

on medical grounds.

(2) A member who is granted medical leave for a period exceeding eighteen

months and is certified by a Medical Board to have no chance to recover pursuant to

subregulation (1) shall not be retained in service beyond the expiry date of his

prescribed period of service, and his Service Chief shall take immediate action, in the

case of—

(a) an officer, to retire or terminate his service; or

(b) a serviceman, to discharge him from the service of the regular

forces,

in accordance with the procedures specified under regulations 42, 43 and 61

respectively.

(3) Notwithstanding the provisions in these Regulations, a member who was

involved in an accident while on duty and sustains injury, loss or deformity of any part

of his body or senses, shall be retained in the service of the regular forces, and if

necessary, his service may be extended, in the case of—

(a) an officer, by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong upon the

recommendation of the Armed Forces Council; and

(b) a serviceman, by the competent authority.

(4) Any extension of service made under subregulation (3) shall not exceed,

in the case of—

(a) an officer, the compulsory retirement age as specified in

regulation 42; and

(b) a serviceman, the period of full time continuous service as

determined by the competent authority.

Member who is undergoing treatment in a hospital

34. (1) A member who has been certified as ill and is undergoing treatment in

any hospital on the date of completion of his prescribed period of service shall be—

(a) retained in the service after such date; and

(b) eligible for pay, allowance and other benefits until the certification

of a Medical Board made under subregulation (2) has been

obtained.

(2) A Medical Board shall be established to study the case of any member

who has been admitted in a hospital to undergo treatment and the period of treatment

in such hospital exceeds six months or any such earlier period, particularly to determine

whether—

(a) such member can be certified as fit and be permitted to be

discharged from the hospital; or

(b) such treatment in the hospital is still required and is reasonable to

be continued for the purpose of recovery of health of such

member; or

(c) any treatment necessary for the recovery of such member may be

obtained from any hospital in or outside Malaysia.

(3) If the Medical Board established under subregulation (2), upon studying

the progress of the treatment provided to such member, makes a certification that such

member has no chance to recover from his illness and is incapable of reporting for duty

upon the expiry of the eighteen months of his period of treatment, his Service Chief shall

take immediate action, in the case of-

(a) an officer, to retire or terminate his service; or

(b) a serviceman, to discharge him from the service of the regular

forces,

on medical grounds in accordance with the procedures specified under regulations 42,

43 and 61 respectively.

In-patient hospital treatment

35. (1) A member who is undergoing in-patient treatment in a hospital shall

continue such treatment to the expiry date of his service.

(2) For the purpose of subregulation (1), a Medical Board shall be established

to determine whether the in-patient hospital treatment should be discontinued or

otherwise, upon the expiry of five months of a member's absence from duty or any such

earlier period.

(3) If a member is undergoing in-patient hospital treatment, he will not be

discharged from the service of the regular forces until an opinion of the Medical Board

under subregulation 34(2) is obtained.

Discharge on medical grounds

36. (1) Action shall be taken to retire or discharge a member from the service of

the regular forces if—

(a) the Medical Board finds that a member who is ill, injured or

suffering from a disease, has no chance to recover and is incapable

of reporting for duty within a period of eighteen months; or

(b) contrary to the earlier opinion of the Medical Board made under

subregulations 34(2) and 35(2), the Medical Board finds that, a

member who has been retained in service has no chance to recover

after the expiry of the period of eighteen months.

(2) Notwithstanding the provisions in subregulation (1), the competent

authority may approve, on the certification of the Medical Board, the retention of

service of a member who has sustained an injury while performing his duty which

results in the loss or impairment of his limbs or essential sensory organs provided that

the service of the member is useful to be continued.

PART III

OFFICERS

Minimum age for commission

37. Any person who wishes to enter into the service of the regular forces shall have

attained the age of eighteen years on the date of such entry to be eligible to be granted a

commission as an officer.

Commissioning of officers

38. (1) Any officer granted a commission by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, upon the

recommendation of the Armed Forces Council, shall enter service as an officer in the

Malaysian Army, the Royal Malaysian Navy or the Royal Malaysian Air Force, as the case

may be.

(2) A commission granted to an officer shall be made in the form of

Commissioning Credentials in accordance with Perintah Majlis Angkatan Tentera.

(3) An officer may be permitted to—

(a) hold a regular commission and shall serve for an indefinite period

of service; or

(b) hold a short service commission and shall serve for a specified

period of service,

in the General Duty List, Professional Duty List or Special Duty List, as determined by

the competent authority.

Extension of service of a short service commissioned officer

39. (1) The period of commission for a short service commissioned officer shall

be in accordance with Perintah Majlis Angkatan Tentera.

(2) A short service commissioned officer may apply, before the completion of

his prescribed period of service, to extend his service in the regular forces.

(3) The period of service for a short service commissioned officer who makes

an application under subregulation (2) may be extended by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong

on the recommendation of the Armed Forces Council if deemed reasonable and

beneficial to the regular forces.

Change of commission

40. (1) A short service commissioned officer may, before the completion of his

prescribed period of service, apply through his Service Chief to change his commission

to a regular commission.

(2) The Yang di-Pertuan Agong may, on the recommendation of the Armed

Forces Council, grant a regular commission to a short service commissioned officer who

applies under subregulation (1), effective from a current date.

Cancellation of commission

41. (1) The Yang di-Pertuan Agong may, on the recommendation of the Armed

Forces Council, cancel the commission of any officer without assigning any reason

therefor.

(2) Any officer whose commission has been cancelled under section 9 of the

Act shall be retired from the service of the regular forces in accordance with

regulation 42.

Retirement of officer

42. (1) Except as otherwise required by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, an officer

shall retire from service in the regular forces upon attaining the compulsory age of

retirement prescribed for his rank as specified in the Third Schedule.

(2) The Yang di-Pertuan Agong may require an officer to be retired from

service in the regular forces—

(a) upon or after he has attained the optional age of retirement

prescribed for his rank as specified in the Fourth Schedule;

(b) in special circumstances, if he is of the rank of Brigadier General or

above although he has not attained the compulsory age of

retirement as specified in subregulation (1) or the optional age of

retirement as specified in paragraph (a);

(c) on medical grounds if he has been certified by a Medical Board as

unfit and incapable of discharging his duties by reason of infirmity

of mind or body which may likely be permanent, whether

connected with duty during his service or otherwise;

(d) if there is no suitable post or prospect of promotion or the officer

is overwhelmed due to unsuitability or inefficiency beyond his

control;

(e) due to his inefficiency or any other reasons within his own control

but not tantamount to a misconduct;

(f) in the interest of the service, when he is charged for an offence

which does not result in his conviction;

(g) due to a misconduct;

(h) at any time, if in the opinion of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong the

circumstances of the case so requires; or

(i) upon him being appointed, with the approval of the Armed Forces

Council, to serve in any organisation in which the Government or

any State Government has an interest.

(3) The Yang di-Pertuan Agong may, on the application of a regular

commissioned officer, allow such officer to retire upon or after the officer has attained

the prescribed optional retirement age.

(4) The retirement under this regulation shall be in accord for the purpose of

determining the grant of pension, gratuity and other benefits as provided in the

regulations made under section 187 of the Act.

Termination of service of a short service commissioned officer

43. (1) The service of a short commissioned officer shall be terminated—

(a) upon the completion of his prescribed period of service; or

(b) if the short service commission period is extended, upon the

completion of the extended period of service.

(2) The Yang di-Pertuan Agong may terminate the service of a short service

commissioned officer—

(a) if he is unfit;

(b) if he is inefficient for reasons beyond his control;

(c) if he is certified by a Medical Board as incapable of discharging his

duties by reason of infirmity of mind or body which may likely be

permanent, whether due to his service or otherwise;

(d) upon attaining the compulsory age of retirement appropriate to his

rank as specified in regulation 42(1);

(e) due to a misconduct ; or

(f) for inefficiency or other causes within his own control but not

amounting to misconduct.

(3) The termination under this regulation shall be in accord for the purpose

of determining the grant of pension, gratuity and other benefits as provided in the

regulations made under section 187 of the Act.

Covering of duties

44. (1) The Service Chief may, if he thinks fit, confer authority to an officer to

cover the duties of another officer holding an equivalent rank or a higher rank than the

former substantive rank as determined by the competent authority in accordance with

the regulations made under section 157 of the Act.

(2) The procedures and any other matters relating to the covering of duties

shall be in accordance with Perintah Majlis Angkatan Tentera.

Acting appointment

45. (1) The competent authority may, if necessary, confer authority to any officer

to fill an appointment which carries with it a higher rank as determined by the

competent authority in accordance with the regulations made under section 157 of the

Act.

(2) The period of conferment of authority for filling an appointment which

carries with it a higher rank shall be reckoned for the purposes of promotion.

(3) The procedures and any other matters relating to the acting appointment

shall be in accordance with Perintah Majlis Angkatan Tentera.

Acting rank

46. (1) The competent authority may, if necessary, confer authority to any officer

to act in an appointment which carries with it a rank higher than the substantive rank.

(2) The procedures and any others matter relating to the acting rank shall be

in accordance with Perintah Majlis Angkatan Tentera.

Reversion to substantive rank

47. An officer holding an acting rank may be reverted to the substantive rank as

directed by the competent authority or the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, as the case may be,

in the circumstances provided in Perintah Majlis Angkatan Tentera.

Promotion

48. For the purpose of section 12 of the Act, the qualifications and criteria for the

promotion of an officer shall be in accordance with Perintah Majlis Angkatan Tentera.

Eligibility for batman

49. (1) The service of a batman shall be made available as follows:

(a) three batmen for the Chief of Armed Forces;

(b) two batmen for each person in the case of the Chief of the Army,

the Chief of the Navy and the Chief of the Air Force;

(c) one batman for each person in the case of a Brigadier General and

above; and

(d) one batman for each person in the case of any officer holding a

commanding officer appointment.

(2) For the purpose of this regulation, "a batman" means a serviceman who

shall be responsible to manage the needs of an officer as specified in subregulation (1)

based on the duties determined by the competent authority, and who shall not be

deemed as a personal servant.

PART IV

SERVICEMEN

Enlistment of apprentice member

50. (1) A person who is below the age of eighteen years may be enlisted as an

apprentice member.

(2) The initial period of service of an apprentice member shall be reckoned

upon him attaining the age of eighteen years.

(3) The terms and conditions of service for an apprentice member shall be in

accordance with Perintah Majlis Angkatan Tentera.

Basic training

51. A serviceman shall, after being enlisted, undergo basic recruit training for a

period of six months or any other period of basic service as determined by the

competent authority.

Period of service

52. (1) The period of full-time service of a serviceman in the regular forces shall

commence from the date of his attestation or when he attains the age of eighteen years,

whichever is the earlier, and such period of service shall be reckoned for the purpose of

promotion and seniority of such serviceman.

(2) A serviceman who enters into the service of the regular forces on or after

the appointed date shall serve—

(a) full-time for a period of twelve years;

(b) if the period of service is extended, for the extended period as

determined by the competent authority; and

(c) for a period of five years in the reserve, provided that his age does

not exceed fifty-five years.

Extension of service

53. (1) A serviceman enlisted in the regular forces may, six months before the

expiry of the period of full-time service, apply to the competent authority to extend his

full-time service—

(a) from the period of twelve years to fifteen years, and if he has not

attained the age of fifty years, serve for a period of five years in the

reserve;

(b) to cover the period of his resettlement course which he may enroll

for if he has not attained the retirement age of fifty-five years; or

(c) to complete his period of full-time service to include any period of

service which cannot be reckoned on a particular ground, provided

that he has not attained the retirement age of fifty-five years.

(2) A serviceman enlisted in the regular forces may, at least six months before

the expiry of his full-time service, apply to the competent authority to extend the service

of such serviceman for—

(a) re-engagement for the period of full-time service extended for

him;

(b) completing his continuous period of full-time service for twenty

one years; or

(c) enabling him to continue to serve as if his period of full-time

service has not expired.

(3) The competent authority for the purpose of subregulations (1) and (2) are

as follows:

(a) the Armed Forces Council, in respect of the extension of

continuous full-time service of a serviceman who has attained the

age of fifty years but has not attained the retirement age of fiftyfive years;

(b) the Service Chief, in respect of the extension of continuous

full-time service for twenty-one years;

(c) the Assistant Chief of Staff of the Member's Service, in respect of

the extension of continuous full-time service exceeding

twenty-one years, provided that the serviceman has not attained

the retirement age of fifty-five years.

(4) Notwithstanding the provisions in these Regulations, no serviceman may

extend his period of full-time service or be permitted for re-engagement if the effect of

such extension or re-engagement requires him to serve after attaining the age of fiftyfive years.

(5) The rules and procedures relating to the extension of service and reengagement shall be in accordance with Perintah Majlis Angkatan Tentera.

Retention in service

54. (1) Notwithstanding any provisions in these Regulations, a serviceman may

be retained in the service of the regular forces exceeding his period of full-time service

for a term not exceeding twelve months.

(2) The Service Chief shall specify the actual period of such retention and

thereafter such serviceman shall be transferred to the reserve in accordance with

section 27 of the Act.

Training as an officer cadet

55. (1) A serviceman may be selected by a Selection Board to undergo training as

an officer cadet and he shall comply with any conditions determined for such purpose

by the competent authority in accordance with Perintah Majlis Angkatan Tentera.

(2) Any serviceman who fails in his training as an officer cadet shall—

(a) be reverted on duty as a serviceman and be granted the rank and

seniority previously held by him before undergoing the training as

officer cadet; and

(b) complete the period of service prescribed for him upon his

enlistment.

Promotion

56. (1) The competent authority may promote any serviceman to a higher rank to

fill any vacancy in the regular forces.

(2) The promotion shall be from a substantive rank to the next higher rank,

unless decided otherwise by the respective Service Chief.

(3) The promotion of a serviceman may take effect retrospectively

commencing from the date he was authorized to act in such higher rank pursuant to

regulation 58.

(4) The qualifications and criteria for promotion of a serviceman shall be in

accordance with Perintah Majlis Angkatan Tentera.

(5) A serviceman may, without being required to act in any duties of the

higher rank as provided under regulation 58, be appointed to the rank of a lance

corporal by a commanding officer with the approval of the Service Chief.

Covering of duties

57. (1) The Service Chief of a serviceman may, if he thinks necessary, confer

authority to a serviceman to perform the duties of another serviceman holding an

equivalent rank, or a rank higher than the rank of such serviceman, and as determined

by the competent authority in accordance with the regulations made under section 157

of the Act.

(2) The period of covering of duties of another serviceman shall not be

reckoned for the purposes of promotion.

(3) The procedures and any other matters relating to such covering of duties

shall be in accordance with Perintah Majlis Angkatan Tentera.

Acting rank

58. (1) The competent authority may, if necessary, confer authority to any

serviceman to act in an appointment which carries with it a rank higher than a

substantive rank.

(2) The procedures and any other matters relating to an acting rank shall be

in accordance with Perintah Majlis Angkatan Tentera.

Reversion to substantive rank

59. A serviceman holding an acting rank may be reverted to his substantive rank as

directed by the competent authority in the circumstances provided in Perintah Majlis

Angkatan Tentera.

Reduction in rank

60. Subject to section 184 of the Act, a serviceman may be reduced in rank from the

substantive rank currently held by him to a lower rank as the competent authority

thinks fit.

Discharge from service

61. (1) The competent authority may, at any time, discharge any serviceman

from the service of the regular forces on the following grounds:

(a) in the case of a recruit, he is unlikely to become an efficient

serviceman;

(b) in the case of a recruit, upon him applying to purchase his

discharge pursuant to section 31 of the Act;

(c) the enlistment of the serviceman is not approved;

(d) the enlistment of the serviceman was not properly made;

(e) the particulars written in the attestation paper during the

enlistment of such serviceman are false;

(f) mercy;

(g) the state of health of such serviceman is lower than the medical

standards as determined under regulation 11;

(h) the lack of a suitable post or the absence of prospects for

promotion or career development for the serviceman in the

regular forces or the abolition of any post in the regular forces;

(i) unfitness or inefficiency of such serviceman which is not

tantamount to a misconduct;

(j) misconduct committed by the serviceman and he has been

convicted;

(k) the serviceman has been sentenced to a discharge or discharge

with disgrace by court-martial;

(l) renunciation or loss of Malaysian citizenship;

(m) the service of the serviceman is no longer required;

(n) in the interest of the service;

(o) with the approval of the Armed Forces Council, upon the

serviceman being appointed to serve in any organisation in which

the Government or any State Government has an interest;

(p) the serviceman is found to be involved in political activities as

prohibited in Perintah Majlis Angkatan Tentera;

(q) the serviceman has completed his period of full-time service in the

regular forces;

(r) the serviceman has been granted a commission as an officer; or

(s) in the opinion of the competent authority, a particular

circumstance requires so.

(2) Notwithstanding any provisions in these Regulations, a warrant officer

who has been reduced to a lower rank may apply to be discharged from the service of

the regular forces and the competent authority, after considering his application, may

discharge such warrant officer pursuant to section 32 of the Act.

(3) The discharge under this regulation shall be in accord for the purpose of

determining the grant of pension, gratuity and other benefits as provided in the

regulations made under section 187 of the Act.

PART V

OFFICERS CADET

Appointment

62. (1) A person who is a Malaysian citizen may be appointed as officer cadet by

the Armed Forces Council.

(2) A person who is below the age of seventeen and a half years shall not be

appointed as an officer cadet without the written consent of his parents or guardian.

Cancellation of appointment

63. (1) The Armed Forces Council may, at any time without assigning any reasons

therefor, cancel the appointment of any officer cadet, and the cancellation shall take

effect on the date determined by the Armed Forces Council.

(2) An officer cadet whose appointment has been cancelled under

subregulation (1) shall be discharged on the date determined by the Armed Forces

Council.

(3) A serviceman who has been selected as an officer cadet under

subregulation 55(1) whose appointment has been cancelled under subregulation (1),

shall be reverted to his previous appointment as a serviceman.

Discharge

64. An officer cadet, other than a serviceman who has been appointed as an officer

cadet—

(a) before the expiration of a period of three months from the date of his

appointment, may apply to the competent authority to purchase his

discharge in accordance with section 10A of the Act; or

(b) after the expiration of a period of three months from the date of

appointment, may apply to the competent authority for discharge in

accordance with Perintah Majlis Angkatan Tentera.

Failure in course in higher education institution

65. (1) An officer cadet who fails in his course in any institution of higher

education shall have his appointment as an officer cadet cancelled and be discharged

from the service of the regular forces, and the competent authority shall be entitled to

claim for compensation from the officer cadet.

(2) An officer cadet who—

(a) is following a course in an institution of higher education;

(b) fails in one academic year; and

(c) is allowed by the relevant institutional authority, with the consent

of the competent authority, to repeat his course,

shall lose his seniority in the regular forces, reckoning the date of his commission as an

officer for the period of repetition.

Application of certain provisions in Part II

66. Regulations 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 22, 24, 25, 27, 30 and 32 in Part II of these

Regulations shall apply mutatis mutandis to an officer cadet.

PART VI

MISCELLANEOUS

Perintah Majlis Angkatan Tentera

67. Any Perintah Majlis Angkatan Tentera issued before the commencement of these

Regulations is valid and shall—

(a) be deemed to have been issued under these Regulations; and

(b) remain in force for the specified purpose thereof until expressly revoked.

Application and reference to Queen's Regulations for the Royal Navy (QRRN)

68. The application and reference to the Queen's Regulations for the Royal Navy

(QRRN) (Terms of Service) 1957 to the Royal Malaysian Navy which was approved by

the competent authority shall cease on the coming into operation of these Regulations.

Revocation and transitional

69. (1) The following regulations are revoked:

(a) the Malay Regiment Regulations 1933 [G.N. 7425/1933];

(b) the Malay Regiment (Enlistment, Extension of Service and

Re-Engagement) Regulations 1960 [L.N. 119/1960];

(c) The Army and Air Force (Terms of Service) Regulations 1961

[L.N. 363/1961];

(d) The Air Force (Enlistment, Extension of Service and

Re-Engagement) Regulations 1962 [L.N. 24/1962]; and

(e) the Navy (Enlistment, Extension of Service and Re-Engagement)

Regulations 1962 [L.N. 23/1962].

(2) Notwithstanding anything contained in subregulation (1), all orders or

other cause papers made or adopted under the revoked regulations, in so far as they are

not inconsistent with these Regulations shall remain in force until expressly revoked.
